title: DiffLens language analyzer static checks output, protocol version 1
description: `<analyzer> check --dir <tree> --timeout <duration> [--cache-dir <folder>]` runs the language's static checkers on one source tree (for Go: go vet, and staticcheck when it is installed) and prints exactly one JSON document matching this schema on stdout, exiting 0 whenever it could report. For an analyzer whose checkers need the project's dependencies, the core first runs `prepare` on a throwaway copy of the tree and checks that copy, so the dependencies are installed (see tests.schema.json); otherwise --dir is a tree shared by other readers. Checkers read the code; a checker that executes project code (ESLint loading its configuration, clippy running build scripts and proc macros) runs in a sandbox of the analyzer's own, with the network off and writes only to a temporary folder and --cache-dir. They must not write inside --dir. --cache-dir is the same per-project folder test runs get, kept between runs (see tests.schema.json); an analyzer with nothing worth keeping there ignores it. A checker that is not installed is reported as unavailable, not as a failure. Logs go to stderr; a non-zero exit means the analyzer itself failed.

checks.description: One entry per checker the language has, installed or not, in a fixed order.

tool.description: Name a developer knows it by, such as "go vet" or "staticcheck".

status.description: clean: ran, found nothing. findings: ran and reported problems. unavailable: not installed. failed: could not run (the code does not compile, a crash); message says why.

message.description: For unavailable and failed: why, in one line. Null otherwise.
The checker's own words, without a severity prefix such as "warning: ".

rule.description: The checker's own code for it, such as "SA4006" or "printf", or null.

severity.description: The checker's own level for it, mapped: error for what the checker reports as an error (a type error, a lint set to deny, go vet's reports), warning for warnings, info for notes, hints and suggestions. Analyzers always write it; the core reads a document without it (kept from before it existed) as warning.
